text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said that a corrective mini-budget later this year was "very probable" but the government would have to wait a few more weeks before deciding if it was absolutely necessary.
"I have already said that a corrective mini-budget is very probable," Prodi told reporters late on Monday night returning to Rome aboard his plane from a visit to German
The remarks were made to journalists on the understanding that they would not be made public until Tuesday morning.
On Monday, Massimo D'Alema, head of the largest party in Prodi's coalition government, said a mini-budget was "inevitable" but will not be huge.
The government is due to decide on the mini-budget in the next few weeks after final 1996 figures are available.

The Il Sole 24 Ore financial newspaper quoted Treasury sources earlier this month as saying that Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi envisioned a mini-budget to cut italy's deficit by 15.0 trillion lire. --Rome newsroom +396-6782501
